bib.title: MultiModal-GPT: A Vision and Language Model for Dialogue with Humans

read.skipped: nothing; pages 6-10 are demo screenshots (Figs 2-8), only captions extract

question: Can OpenFlamingo be cheaply fine-tuned into a multi-round dialogue model that follows vision-and-language instructions?
hypothesis: Joint training on language-only and vision-language instructions with one unified template, using high-quality long-response data, improves dialogue ability.
contributions: MultiModal-GPT, OpenFlamingo fine-tuned with LoRA in self-attention, cross-attention and FFN of the language decoder
A unified instruction template for language-only and vision-language data
Observation that short-response datasets harm dialogue, and that joint language-only training helps

method.summary: OpenFlamingo (CLIP vision encoder, perceiver resampler, LLaMA decoder with gated cross-attention) is frozen and LoRA adapters are trained on a mix of language-only and vision-language instruction data in one template, with loss on the response and EOS only. Evaluation is qualitative demos only.
method.task: multimodal instruction tuning for multi-turn dialogue

datasets.name: Dolly 15k
datasets.source: language-only instruction data (Peng et al. 2023 cited)

datasets.name: COCO Caption
datasets.preprocessing: GPT-4 generated instructions (list of 10 in Table 3, e.g. 'Can you describe the image?')

datasets.name: VQA v2.0, OKVQA, GQA, CLEVR, NLVR
datasets.preprocessing: tried in preliminary experiments and excluded from the final version

models.name: MultiModal-GPT
models.architecture: OpenFlamingo: CLIP vision encoder + perceiver resampler + LLaMA decoder with gated cross-attention; LoRA on self-attention, cross-attention and FFN

training.objective: next-token prediction; loss only on {response} and <EOS>
training.batch_size: 256 aggregate (1 per GPU, 8 GPUs, update every 16 iterations)

other.iteration: each iteration holds one vision-language pair and one language-only sample
other.note: inferred: 1 per GPU x 8 GPUs x 16 steps x 2 samples = 256, matching the stated aggregate

eval.protocol: No quantitative evaluation; qualitative demos in Figs 2-8.

evidence.quote: Each iteration encompasses one vision-language pair and one language-only instruction data. Consequently, the aggregate batch size amounts to 256.

results.claim: Datasets with one- or two-word answers (VQA v2.0, OKVQA, GQA, CLEVR, NLVR) made the model answer any instruction in one or two words, so they were dropped; no metric or ablation is reported.
results.quote: we observed that the quality of certain datasets, including VQA v2.0 [3], OKVQA [9], GQA [5], CLEVR [6], and NLVR [15], was suboptimal.

results.claim: Joint training with language-only instruction data under the same template is said to improve dialogue, shown only by demos.
results.setup: Dolly 15k and Alpaca GPT4 mixed with vision-language data.
results.quote: Utilizing the same instruction template for both types of data results in a significant improvement in dialogue performance.

results.setup: 8 A100 GPUs, per-GPU batch 1, accumulation over 16 iterations, 1 epoch.
results.quote: Consequently, the aggregate batch size amounts to 256.

results.claim: Training sample from A-OKVQA is 5000 pairs; 512 each for COCO Caption and OCR VQA.
results.setup: Random samples; LLaVA and Mini-GPT4 used in full.
results.quote: we include a random sample of 5000 image-text pairs from the A-OKVQA dataset and 512 image-text pairs each from the COCO Caption and OCR VQA datasets

limits: No quantitative evaluation or ablation; all evidence is qualitative demos.
Dataset-quality finding comes from unreported preliminary runs.
